title: The Secret to No-Channeling Espresso: Puck Prep Essentials
summary: Learn the essential techniques of WDT, distribution, and tamping to eliminate channeling and improve your shot consistency.
body:
The Importance of Puck Prep

Even with the most expensive espresso machine, poor puck preparation leads to channeling—where water finds the path of least resistance through the coffee bed. This results in an uneven extraction, giving you a shot that is both sour and bitter at the same time.

Step 1: WDT (Weiss Distribution Technique)

Using a WDT tool with thin needles (0.3mm to 0.4mm) helps break up clumps caused by the grinder's static and ensures an even density across the portafilter basket. Swirl the needles from the bottom up to homogenize the bed.

Step 2: Leveling

Before tamping, ensure the coffee is level. A quick vertical tap on the counter can help settle the grounds, but your WDT tool should have already done the heavy lifting.

Step 3: The Tamp

A level tamp is far more important than the specific amount of pressure you apply. Once the air is squeezed out of the coffee bed, additional pressure doesn't change the density significantly. Focus on keeping the tamper perfectly horizontal to the basket rim.
